name: Daylio
one_liner: Daylio is a simple, visual mood tracker that lets you log your mood and activities without writing, helping you identify patterns in what affects your emotional state.
best_for: People who want quick, simple mood tracking without journaling
Those who prefer visual/icon-based apps over text-heavy ones
People wanting to identify connections between activities and mood
Those who struggle to maintain consistent journaling habits
People with depression or mood disorders tracking patterns
not_for: Those wanting in-depth written journaling features
People looking for CBT exercises or therapeutic interventions
short_description: Simple mood tracker using icons instead of words. Track mood and activities to find patterns. No writing required.
long_description: Daylio is a mood tracking app designed for people who don't like writing. Instead of journaling, you select a mood icon and tap which activities you did that day. Over time, Daylio shows you patterns: which activities correlate with better moods, how your mood changes over weeks and months, and what your baseline mood looks like. It's fast (under 30 seconds per entry) and gamified with streaks and achievements.
patient_summary: Daylio makes mood tracking as easy as tapping a few icons. See which activities make you feel better or worse, track your moods over time, and spot patterns you might not notice otherwise.

pricing.notes: Free version includes core tracking. Premium adds unlimited history, advanced stats, and export.

privacy.notes: Data stored locally by default. Optional cloud backup available. Export your data anytime.

faqs.q: How is Daylio different from journaling apps?
faqs.a: Daylio uses icons instead of writing. You tap a mood face, tap which activities you did, and you're done in under 30 seconds. It's designed for people who struggle to maintain written journal habits.

faqs.q: Can Daylio actually help with depression?
faqs.a: Mood tracking alone isn't treatment for depression, but it can help you understand your patterns, identify triggers, and notice what activities help. Many therapists recommend mood tracking as part of treatment.

faqs.q: Is Daylio better than eMoods for bipolar?
faqs.a: For bipolar disorder specifically, eMoods is better because it tracks both depression and elevation on separate scales. Daylio tracks one overall mood which doesn't capture the bipolar experience as well.

faqs.q: Can I export my Daylio data?
faqs.a: Yes. Daylio lets you export your data in PDF or CSV format. You can share these reports with a therapist or keep them for your records. Premium offers more export options.

how_clinicians_use_it: Assign as homework for patients to track mood between sessions
Have patients export reports to review together in session
Help patients identify activity-mood patterns to target in treatment
Monitor treatment progress through mood trends over time
clinician.implementation_notes: No clinician dashboard - patient shares exports manually. PDF and CSV export available. Consider for patients who find journaling overwhelming.
